title: Isolated locally finite type points become finite after an etale base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let $s\in S$ and let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in X$ satisfy $f(x_i)=s$. Let $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and assume that $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and that each $x_i$ is an isolated point of $X_s$. Then there are an etale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S,s)$ (so $U$ is a scheme, $U\to S$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $u\in U$ maps to $s$), integers $m_i\geq0$, and open subschemes $V_{i,j}\subseteq X\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] such that: each $V_{i,j}\to U$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; it has a unique point $v_{i,j}$ over $u$ with $\kappa(u)\subseteq\kappa(v_{i,j})$ a finite purely inseparable extension [def-weil-residue-field] [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]; $v_{i,j}$ maps to $x_i$; no other point of $(X\times_SU)_u$ maps to $x_i$; and $v_{i,j}=v_{i',j'}$ implies $(i,j)=(i',j')$.
